question_text: An empty hamster cage has mass $800\text{ g}$. When $5$ hamsters are placed in the cage, the total mass is $1400\text{ g}$.

subparts.stem: Find the average mass of the hamsters in the cage.

mark_breakdown.desc: Subtracting cage mass from total mass and dividing by number of hamsters

subparts.solution:
$$\text{Average mass} = \frac{\text{total mass} - \text{mass of cage}}{\text{number of hamsters}}$$
$$= \frac{1400 - 800}{5}$$
$$= \frac{600}{5}$$
$$= 120\text{ g}$$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Average mass per hamster is found by dividing the net mass of all hamsters by the total number of hamsters.
step_by_step: Find the total mass of the 5 hamsters by subtracting the cage mass from the gross mass: $1400 - 800 = 600\text{ g}$.
Divide by the number of hamsters: $\frac{600}{5} = 120\text{ g}$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Forgetting to subtract the mass of the cage before dividing by 5.

subparts.stem: Hence write an arithmetic sequence for $u_n$, the approximate total mass when $n$ hamsters are placed in the cage.

mark_breakdown.desc: Stating the linear model / general term $u_n = 800 + 120n$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The total mass forms an arithmetic sequence with initial mass (cage) as the intercept and the average mass per hamster as the common difference.
step_by_step: Identify the constant base mass: $800\text{ g}$.
Identify the rate of increase per hamster: $120\text{ g}$.
Combine into the general term formula: $u_n = 800 + 120n$.
